venous_boundary_advantages.advantage: Venous pressure as drug clearance predictor
venous_boundary_advantages.description: P_venous directly affects drainage rate → directly affects drug clearance rate. VP shunts drain to peritoneum (different pressure, different clearance).
venous_boundary_advantages.quantifiable: Drug clearance = f(P_venous, R_shunt). CereVasc can model this; VP shunt manufacturers cannot.

venous_boundary_advantages.description: If drug delivery is coordinated with venous pressure cycles (e.g., respiration-induced venous pressure variation), delivery can be timed to minimize drug loss.
venous_boundary_advantages.quantifiable: Respiratory variation in P_venous (~2-3 mmHg) creates windows of lower clearance.

venous_boundary_advantages.advantage: Closed-loop: estimate CSF drug concentration from P_CSF + P_venous + Q_drainage
venous_boundary_advantages.description: The eShunt's known hydraulic relationship (P_CSF → valve → P_venous) allows estimation of drug clearance rate, which allows adaptive dosing.
venous_boundary_advantages.quantifiable: Estimated clearance = Q_drainage / CSF_volume × (1 - retention_factor). Only possible with known venous boundary.

venous_boundary_advantages.advantage: Spatial separation: drug delivery proximal, drainage distal
venous_boundary_advantages.description: The endovascular anatomy (subarachnoid → dural venous sinus) provides a natural spatial gradient. Drug delivered proximally (subarachnoid) has residence time before reaching the venous drain.
venous_boundary_advantages.quantifiable: Residence time = shunt_length / (Q_drainage / cross_section_area). VP shunts don't have this spatial gradient.

vp_shunt_comparison.eShunt_drains_to: dural venous sinus (known pressure, measured boundary)
vp_shunt_comparison.advantage: eShunt's venous boundary is a MEASURED, MODELED, and CONTROLLABLE variable. VP shunt's peritoneal boundary is none of these.
vp_shunt_comparison.moat_strength: The invention requires the venous boundary as a load-bearing element. VP shunts cannot replicate this.
